newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BROKER DE POSSON CEASES ACTIVITIES.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BROKER DE POSSON CEASES ACTIVITIES.

text.p: Belgian brokerage De Posson & Cie said on Tuesday that after more than 20 years it had decided to cease activities as from Wednesday.

"Today, despite a restructuring plan, taking into account the uncertainties about the future of the profession...we have asked for the withdrawal of our licence as a broker in financial instruments," it said in a statement.
Watchdog the Banking and Finance Commission had accepted the request with effect from Wednesday, June 4, De Posson said.

De Posson said that in the past 18 months its shareholders had injected "important amounts" of money and deposited additional guarantees to preserve jobs and the quality of services. "No solution assuming the continuation of activities could be found," it said on Tuesday.

Almost a year ago De Posson withdrew as inter primary dealer broker (IPDB), but planned to continue offering its services as government bond (OLO) broker to the 15 primary dealers of Belgian state debt.
The move came after De Posson threatened to resign if the primary dealers did not commit themselves to channelling more trading volume through the firm.

The function of IPDB, quoting two-way prices in OLOs to primary dealers exclusively to boost market liquidity, was created in May 1995. The IPDB system was hit by sharp competition from London brokers.
